constraint_decided_it: S22 Segment of Matter's scope note ('The defining spatial extent is typically declared on a continuous matter ... It may however be extracted at some point in time along the declared boundaries'; uncorrupted subsections 'may continue to exist as segments of matter in their own right') directly contradicts B's stated ground for rejecting the CRMsci route, and Issue 720 (register: 'a new example for P46 and E13, P140, P141, P177', proposing the Lewis Chessmen example and replacing the Fosseway example) says nothing about 'discomfort with over-literal P46 examples' or that P46 'should be used carefully'. Everything both answers assert about the headline choice is licensed by the same two texts: E19's 'physical boundaries that separate them completely in an objective way from other objects' / 'may be purely administrative' and the Monotonicity principle ('if experts enter subsequently correct statements ... the system should not regard any results from those statements as invalid'), so identity did not separate them; source fidelity and class specificity did.
better_modelling: Two objects, no merge, and the old accession numbers stand. Each segment stays an E19 Physical Object -- a unit for documentation with objective physical boundaries -- keeping the P1/P48 identifier assigned by its own crew's E15 Identifier Assignment; monotonicity means the loan paperwork needs no migration. The material layer is where the new fact belongs, and CRMsci is written for exactly this: S11's scope note names 'the sequence of layers of a bore core' and S13 Sample names 'the layering of a bore core', while S2 Sample Taking's scope note says the removed matter 'may acquire a persistent identity of different nature ... such as becoming a physical object in the narrower sense' -- which is precisely the E19/S13 dual layer. So each core is an S13 Sample removed by an S2 Sample Taking (O5 removed: S2 -> S13) that was O3 sampled from (S2 -> S10) the same fault-zone body modelled as S22 Segment of Matter (S22 subclass of S20 subclass of E26 subclass of E18 subclass of S10, so the range holds); shared origin is then a consequence of the two sample-takings pointing at one S10, which is sharper than A's bare O25 contains. Finally, because this is a stratigrapher's reading of fifty-year-old logs and not an observation, the join is an I2 Belief concluded by an I5 Inference Making (J2 concluded that) -- the SIG's own resolution closing Issue 544 says reassembling separately catalogued fragments 'is not much different from the reasoning involved in archaeological restorations, or rearranging sherds, or statues, buildings, papyri' and 'should be a more generic construct expressed in CRMinf'. Note that I5's premises must be I2 Beliefs (J1 used as premise: I5 -> I2), not the E31 core logs themselves; the logs attach via P70 documents to the beliefs' subject matter.
reasoning: Both answers reach the modelling the CRM prescribes on the question actually asked -- two E19 documentation units, no retroactive merge, accession identifiers preserved under monotonicity -- and both check out on domain and range (A: O25 S10->S10 with S13 and S22 both subclasses of S10; B: P46 E18->E18, whose scope note explicitly 'does not specify when and for how long a component element resided in the respective whole', so a former-part assertion is legitimate). A is suboptimal because it stops at the material layer: it never models the interpretive status of the stratigrapher's claim, and it reaches for O25 contains where CRMsci provides the purpose-built S2/O5/O3 sample-taking path, but every quotation it makes is real (t1080 message 4, Martin Doerr, verbatim 'without loosing their identity'; S11's 'sequence of layers of a bore core'; P130's 'this process should be explicitly modelled'; E19's 'purely administrative', which A softens to 'often' where the text says 'may be'). B is unsupported because two of its cited sources do not say what it claims -- Issue 720 is a proposal to swap in the Lewis Chessmen example, not a caution about P46, and S22's scope note provides for extraction rather than excluding it -- and that second misreading is load-bearing, since it is the reason B discards S11/S13, the classes whose scope notes name bore cores by name. B's Issue 544 citation is exact and is the single best piece of evidence in either answer; A wins only on the harsher verdict, not on insight.
